text: Given valid credentials, when the agent calls initialize then tools/list, then the response lists 14 tools, every name starts with intercom_, and each description is a single verb-first sentence
Given a request with X-Intercom-Access-Token missing, when any intercom_* tool is called, then the response is HTTP 401 with code not_configured and the message names the missing header

Given valid credentials, when intercom_search_contacts is called with a known email on a live workspace, then that contact is returned; a bogus email returns an empty list with has_more false, not an error
steps: Obtain a real Intercom Personal Access Token for a test workspace
Call intercom_search_contacts with email=<a known seeded contact's email>
expect: First call returns the known contact's id and email; second call returns an empty contacts array with has_more=false and no error envelope
evidence: needs a real vendor account; no Intercom test workspace available to this pipeline run

text: Given valid credentials, when intercom_get_conversation is called on a known conversation id, then the conversation is returned including its conversation_parts thread
steps: With a real Intercom workspace, note a conversation id with at least 2 replies
expect: Response includes the conversation and a conversation_parts list with every reply in order

text: Given valid credentials, when intercom_create_contact is called with a new email, then a contact is created in the tenant's real Intercom workspace and the tool returns its id
steps: Call intercom_create_contact with a fresh, not-previously-used email
Open the Intercom UI for the same workspace and search that email
expect: Tool response id matches the contact now visible in Intercom's own UI

text: Given valid credentials, when intercom_reply_conversation is called with message_type comment vs note, then a public reply (visible to the customer) or an internal note (not visible to the customer) is posted respectively
steps: Open the conversation in Intercom's UI
expect: The comment reply is shown as visible to the end customer; the note is shown as an internal-only note

text: Given a mocked Intercom response of 401/404/422/429/5xx, when a tool call receives it, then the error envelope code matches (unauthorized/not_found/invalid_argument/rate_limited/upstream_error) and a 429 is retried with backoff before surfacing
Given no X-Intercom-Region header, when a read tool is called against a US-region workspace, then the call succeeds using the default US API host
steps: Call any read tool (e.g. intercom_list_admins) with only X-Intercom-Access-Token set, no region header
Confirm the workspace used is a standard US-region Intercom account
expect: Call succeeds (200-level result), connector used https://api.intercom.io
evidence: needs a real vendor account (US workspace)

text: Given two simulated concurrent requests carrying different X-Intercom-Access-Token values, when both are handled at the same time, then neither request's token or response data is observable from the other
Given no Intercom credentials configured anywhere, when GET /health is called, then it returns 200 (health check never depends on upstream reachability)
